In Figure Yi, there is longitude line b in the middle, latitude line n below, and the intersection point of the day-night boundary on the right side with the right boundary of the frame is labeled F; F is clearly higher than E in Figure Jia, close to the upper-right part.
Reasoning: The question stem states that the two figures are day-night distributions at the same moment, and that the map sheet areas are the same, but the scales are different. According to the specified comparison method, looking at the form from the central longitude lines a and b to the intersection points E and F of the day-night boundary at the right boundary, the position of F in Figure Yi is higher than E in Figure Jia, indicating that within the same width on the map, Figure Yi includes a larger actual longitude range; conversely, Figure Jia includes a smaller actual longitude range. Scale equals the ratio of distance on the map to actual distance. Under the condition that the map sheet areas are the same, the smaller the actual range represented, the larger the scale. Therefore, the scale of Figure Jia is larger.
